message:
docs(update): put the three defects in the ledger, and correct what needs a real machine

I09, I10 and I11 record what the one-line diagnosis turned up. I10 is the one worth reading twice:
a payload default written as L"ui\shell.html" where \s is not an escape, so the value was
"uishell.html" and a shipped updater would have looked for two files that do not exist -- every
swap failing, and only in the field. The compiler said nothing; a Python one-liner over the same
string warned about it.

The unverified list gains a line for the client backup whose lifetime is still unexplained, since
the assertions around it were narrowed and someone reading only that document should know.

And the claim that the execution layer could only be checked on a real machine is corrected. It
was wrong: copying, starting processes, job objects and relaunching are all exercised in isolation
now, against dummy executables in temp directories. What genuinely needs a real machine is
operational service registration, an operational certificate chain, and the UAC experience.
Deferring the execution layer to a field test means that code does not run until release, which is
precisely how the defects in this work survived as long as they did.

Documentation only.
